title: Women's changing roles in wartime

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches women's wartime roles: the closest, Women between the wars, covers the 1920s and only mentions the war in passing, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Women's changing roles in wartime
card: As men left to fight, women were needed in new places. Many joined the armed services, such as the Australian Women's Army Service, and the Women's Land Army, which put women to work on farms.
Women also took factory jobs once done by men, making goods such as munitions, uniforms and aircraft parts.
Women were usually paid less than men for the same kind of work. Wages were set at a lower rate.
These changes were meant to last only until the war ended. Afterwards, many women were expected to return to their earlier roles and give their jobs back to returning men.
draft.remember: War opened new work to women, but at lower pay and mostly for the war years only.

a.q: Why did many women take up factory and farm work in wartime Australia?
opts: Men had left to fight, so workers were needed
Women were paid more than men for the same work
The government meant the changes to be permanent
Women had already held most of these jobs before
a.why: Men leaving for the services created gaps in the workforce that women filled. Pay was not higher for women, as they were usually paid less than men.
a.clue: Think about who was away from home.

b.q: Grace joined a munitions factory in Adelaide in 1943. In 1946 she was told her job was going to a returned soldier. Which idea does this best show?
opts: Women's wartime jobs were often seen as temporary
Women's wages rose above men's after the war
Factories stopped making goods after the war
Women had refused to work in factories
b.why: Grace's loss of her job to a returned soldier shows that wartime work was expected to last only until the war ended. Her case says nothing about women being paid more than men.
b.clue: Who was given the job back?

a.best: Men had left to fight, so workers were needed

b.best: Women's wartime jobs were often seen as temporary

problems.detail: The right option is the only one with a qualifier ("often"), while the wrong options are flat absolute claims. This lets a student pick it without knowing the idea.
